title: Jantar Mantar 2.0 — CJP / anti-SIR protest, Delhi
summary: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth movement, along with Left groups, student unions and civil-society groups, called a protest at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi, on Sat 10 Oct 2026. They want Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls scrapped. Critics say SIR has removed more than 130 million names (NPR/AP). Delhi Police refused permission and locked down central Delhi: BNSS Sec 163 orders, about 45 metro stations shut until gates reopened around 10:36 PM, trains cancelled, internet cut within 4 km, and roughly 23,000 CAPF personnel deployed. Police detained CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on board their flight. YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was detained at his Gurugram home. Opposition leaders, lawyers and journalists were also detained. INDIA bloc street protests have been running since about 2 Oct, and Rahul Gandhi was detained on 6 and 7 Oct.

stats.label: Detained in Delhi today (media)
stats.note: The Hindu (6:53 PM) restates that over 5,000 protesters were detained in Delhi, including CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, CPI(M) leaders and student activists. Delhi Police said at 6:53 PM they have begun releasing detainees (a senior officer via The Hindu); no count of releases given. NDTV (7:41 PM, with PTI inputs): over 1,500 detained across Delhi; many were released later in the evening. Scroll (8:16 PM): police reportedly detained more than 7,000 protesters in Delhi. NDTV (~10 PM): at least 3,000 detained across Delhi; most released by night. Delhi Police sources via ANI (9:38 PM): all detainees released from detention centres except CJP leaders, for whom due legal process will be followed. As of 10:05 PM. ThePrint (5:28 PM): around 3,500 detained in Delhi; police say detentions could last 'up to 24 hours'. Officials told PTI at 4:53 PM that Delhi Police detained over 3,000 people during the protest (The Hindu's summary says 3,300; The Tribune says 3,000). A Delhi Police officer told The Hindu around 5,000 were detained till 2 PM. TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee claimed (ANI, ~5:07 PM) about 2,500 were detained. A Delhi Police officer told The Hindu around 5,000 protesters were detained across Delhi till 2 PM and taken to temporary detention facilities (The Hindu live blog, 2:57 PM entry; Scroll repeated it at ~4:45 PM). Earlier figures: TOI 1,500+ (midday); PTI citing police sources ~1,000 (3:57 PM). Outside Delhi: Chennai 100+ (NDTV, ~4:22 PM); Bengaluru at least 50 AISA students at Freedom Park (The Hindu, 3:21 PM); Mumbai: over 400 detained so far at August Kranti Maidan (Mumbai Police via ANI, 5:39 PM; PTI had ~200 at 5:18 PM); actor Imran Khan and his relative Zayn Marie Khan were among those detained (NDTV, 8:30 PM); Pune: about 80–100 detained at Lal Mahal Chowk and taken to Lashkar police station (IANS, 8:46 PM); earlier Scroll reported detentions with no number. HT (10:47 PM): police say nearly 4,000 detained. As of 11:10 PM. NDTV (12:12 AM headline): at least 3,000 were detained in Delhi and all of them were released except the CJP leaders and Dhruv Rathee. NDTV also reports at least 25,000 police and paramilitary personnel were deployed. As of 12:15 AM. Over 7,000 released per police sources (DNA, 8:00 AM; ET Now, ~7:19 AM). ET Now says all 7,000 were released except Abhijeet Dipke, Dhruv Rathee and two others. DNA, citing police sources, says Dipke and Das remain in custody. CJP claims more than 15,000 people, including students, civil society members and political leaders, faced detention and police action (Indian Express; CJP claim). Police sources told Indian Express that detainees were kept at around 30 detention centres. As of 8:15 AM. Correction, 10:05 AM: Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released at about 10 AM on an Executive Magistrate's order (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench). Dhruv Rathee was released at about 3 AM (Hindustan Times, PTI). That corrects the morning reports that still had them in custody. As of 10:05 AM. HT (11:40 AM, 11 Oct): an estimated 7,000 people were detained on Saturday. As of 12:05 PM.

stats.label: Detained nationwide (CJP claim)
stats.note: Figure from CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka on 8–9 Oct, before the protest. Not verified independently.

stats.label: SFI members detained (SFI claim)
stats.note: SFI national president Adarsh M Saji told PTI more than 400 members were detained after their march began around 10 AM. Not verified independently.

stats.label: Released today
stats.note: A group of lawyers detained near the Supreme Court were released after the CJI stepped in (about 2:30 PM). Senior Advocate Shadan Farasat was released (Bar & Bench, 6:51 PM). Pinarayi Vijayan was released (PTI, ~7:10 PM). ANI reported Ratna Singh's release at about 5:53 PM, but The Hindu says she posted at 7:13 PM that she was still detained; the reports conflict. 6:53 PM: Delhi Police say they have initiated the release of protesters (a senior officer via The Hindu); no count given. 7:11 PM: women released from Maidan Garhi police station (The Wire). 7:38 PM: police sources say women and senior citizens are being released first (The Hindu); many detainees were released in the evening (NDTV). 8:09 PM: Mamata Banerjee released (ANI). 8:13 PM: Arvind Kejriwal released from Jaffarpur police station (PTI). 8:30 PM: Neha Bora and the women detained with her released from Maidan Garhi police station (India Today). No overall release count given. 9:18 PM: police sources say most of those detained today have been released (IANS). 9:38 PM: Delhi Police sources say all detainees were released from detention centres except CJP leaders (ANI). 9:20 PM: Pinarayi Vijayan, John Brittas and K.N. Balagopal released from Mandir Marg police station (IANS). 9:35 PM: Yogendra Yadav says he was released from Maidangarhi police station (his own post). 9:59 PM: about 150 people picked up from Gurudwara Bangla Sahib were released from Chhatrasal Stadium (Scroll). No overall release count given. 11 Oct: Dhruv Rathee released at about 3 AM and handed to his family (Hindustan Times, PTI, citing officials). Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka released at about 10 AM on an Executive Magistrate's order at Delhi Cantt Police Station (LiveLaw, citing Ratna Singh; Bar & Bench).

stats.label: Named key figures still held
stats.note: Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released at about 10 AM on 11 Oct on an Executive Magistrate's order at Delhi Cantt Police Station (LiveLaw, 9:58 AM, citing Ratna Singh; Bar & Bench, 10:00 AM). Dhruv Rathee was released at about 3 AM and handed to his family (Hindustan Times and PTI, citing officials). This corrects earlier "still in custody" reports, including ETV Bharat, ET Now and this page's 8:15 AM update. Senior Advocate Dinesh Dwivedi: no new report. Ratna Singh was at the production as CJP's lawyer; an outlet has not confirmed when her own detention ended. Fidal Tom and students Saurabh, Nikhil and Harsh were released overnight (The Wire). The earlier "at least 12" figure counted named people whose individual status was already unconfirmed or likely released. As of 10:05 AM IST. The three were released on a one-year condition that they not breach the peace, with a Rs 50,000 surety, according to LiveLaw citing Ratna Singh, PTI, and Delhi Police via ANI. Dhruv Rathee later said he was kidnapped and gave no undertaking (Hindustan Times, his claim). The Hindu says he was released around 2 AM; HT and PTI say about 3 AM. As of 12:05 PM IST.

detainees.status: RELEASED (~3 AM, 11 Oct). Hindustan Times (11:47 AM) reports his Instagram caption: "I was not arrested or detained, I was KIDNAPPED." HT says he gave no undertaking to Gurugram Police. His claim. The Hindu (10:53 AM) says the Gurugram Crime Branch released him around 2 AM. HT and PTI, citing officials, say about 3 AM. Both times are kept. HT's 11:47 AM story says he was detained around 9:30 AM on Saturday. HT's earlier story said about 7:30 AM. Both accounts are kept. Hindustan Times, citing officials, says Dhruv Rathee was released at 3 AM on Sunday and handed over to his family. He had been picked up from his residence in Kendriya Vihar society, Gurugram Sector 56, around 7:30 AM on Saturday. An unnamed police officer, quoted by PTI, said: "He can be detained again, or further legal action might be taken if he tries to go to Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders." This corrects earlier reports that he was still in custody, including ETV Bharat (6:48 AM) and ET Now (~7:19 AM). Earlier account: Taken to an undisclosed place in Gurugram. No release reported NDTV (~10 PM) says he remained in custody, with Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Delhi Police sources (ANI, 9:38 PM) said detainees other than CJP leaders had been released. No outlet has reported a release as of 11:10 PM. NDTV (~10 PM) still has him in custody. Social claims of a release are unverified and contradicted by NDTV. Arvind Kejriwal (his own post, 10:03 PM) asked the Prime Minister where Dipke, Ranka, Rathee and Das are being held. HT (11:25 PM) says he is still held, with Dipke, Das and Ranka, while everyone else was released. NDTV says he remained in custody as of 12:15 AM. Social posts claiming he is out are unverified and contradicted by NDTV. LawBeat says a Supreme Court habeas plea also names him; Bar & Bench's report does not mention him (single source). That plea was filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity, not by CJP. CJP says it did not file or approve it, and Bharti has sought to withdraw it.

detainees.name: Abhijeet Dipke
detainees.when: 10 Oct, about 10:30 AM IST (ThePrint live blog)
detainees.where: On board an Air India flight from Mumbai, just after landing at IGI Airport, Delhi. Later moved to Gurugram (TOI)
detainees.reason: Protest was banned / had no permission. No written grounds reported
detainees.status: RELEASED (~10 AM, 11 Oct). An Executive Magistrate ordered the release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka at Delhi Cantt Police Station (LiveLaw, 9:58 AM, citing CJP legal head Ratna Singh; Bar & Bench, 10:00 AM, which reports them released). This corrects earlier reports, including this page's 8:15 AM update, that they were still in custody. LiveLaw (10:20 AM), citing Ratna Singh, says they were released on condition they will not engage in a breach of the peace for one year. PTI (10:54 AM) says the condition is that they "maintain peace" for one year. Delhi Police, via ANI (10:56 AM), say the preventive arrest was under BNSS Sections 126 and 170 on 10 Oct 2026, that all due legal procedures were followed, that they were produced before the Special Executive Magistrate's court at Delhi Cantt, and that a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was taken. That is the police account. CJP counsel Soutik Banerjee said at 10:18 AM that all three had been released (LiveLaw). Indian Express (10:51 AM) says they walked out of Delhi Cantt police station. Delhi Police had placed the three under preventive arrest under BNSS Sections 126 (security for keeping the peace) and 170 (arrest to prevent the commission of cognisable offences) (LiveLaw, 8:23 AM; Bar & Bench, 8:32 AM; PTI, 9:10 AM; Indian Express, 9:34 AM). They were produced before the Special Executive Magistrate, South West District, at Delhi Cantt Police Station (LiveLaw, 9:35 AM; Bar & Bench, 9:39 AM; ANI video, 9:51 AM). India Today (9:00 AM, police sources) had said that no arrests had been made. His mother, Anita Dipke, said he was not allowed to attend his grandmother's funeral (PTI video, 11:12 AM). He was in Delhi until about 10 AM. After release he wrote, as reported by Hindustan Times and The Wire: "Modi, as PM, is an embarrassment to India. Never has this country seen a bigger coward and bully." His words. Hindustan Times says the three were held from inside the plane: flight AI 2428 landed at 10:18 AM on Saturday and was moved to remote bay R12 (people aware of the matter, per HT). Earlier account: CJP alleges he has no access to lawyers. His grandmother died in Hingoli the same day Police sources (PTI, ~4:06 PM) say he was told of his grandmother's death and left to decide whether to stay or go home for her last rites. Delhi Police (via ANI, ~4:26 PM) say he was offered help to travel home on humanitarian grounds for his grandmother's funeral. At 1:08 PM, intelligence sources told The Hindu that Dipke, Das and Ranka were taken to three different locations in Delhi-NCR. CJP said at ~4:45 PM it still has no information on Dipke, Das and Ranka's whereabouts and is concerned for their safety. 5:20 PM: CJP publicly appealed to Delhi Police to release Dipke immediately, saying his whereabouts are still unknown, his lawyers cannot reach him and his family cannot tell him of his grandmother's death (CJP claim). This conflicts with police sources earlier saying he was informed; both accounts are kept, attributed. Delhi Police (via IANS, 7:12 PM) say Dipke's grandmother's death was promptly conveyed to him with due sensitivity, he was told the funeral time, and he was offered all possible assistance to travel home. NDTV (7:41 PM) says that by evening it was not clear whether he would be released. CJP said at a 7:35 PM press conference it still has no information on the whereabouts of Dipke, Das and Ranka (The Hindu). Police sources (The Hindu, 7:38 PM) say due legal process will be followed in the case of CJP leaders. Ajinkya Shinde (CJP, ~8:55 PM) alleges police did not let Dipke speak to his lawyer or family after news of his grandmother's death. CJP says Dipke, Das and Ranka were taken to different locations across Delhi-NCR (The Hindu; IANS, 9:04 PM). SFI joint secretary Aishe Ghosh demanded their release (The Hindu, 8:35 PM). NDTV (~10 PM) says Dipke, Das, Ranka and Dhruv Rathee remained in custody. Delhi Police sources (ANI, 9:38 PM): all detainees were released from detention centres except CJP leaders, and due legal process will be followed for the CJP leaders. 10:47 PM: Hindustan Times reports Delhi Police posted on X that Dipke was "immediately" told of his grandmother's death and the funeral time and was offered "possible facilitation" to travel home; CJP replied, "Where is Abhijeet? His family wants to talk to him... last rites tomorrow morning." 10:53 PM: CJP posted, "It's been 12 hours. No information. No accountability," and demanded immediate release, disclosure of whereabouts and access to lawyers for Dipke, Das and Ranka. NDTV says police told Dipke he could leave for his grandmother's funeral, but it is unclear whether he will be released. Nothing new was reported on that beyond the earlier police and CJP accounts. HT (11:25 PM) says Dipke, Das, Ranka and Dhruv Rathee are still held while everyone else was released. NDTV says the four remained in custody as of 12:15 AM, and that everyone else among at least 3,000 detainees was released. Ajinkya Shinde wrote to the Delhi Police Commissioner at 11:29 PM asking where Dipke, Das and Ranka are (IANS). A habeas corpus plea seeking their production and release was filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity, not by CJP. CJP legal cell chief Ratna Singh posted at 12:48 AM: "This petition is not filed by @Cockroachisback. We are not approaching the Supreme Court, and no habeas corpus petition has been approved by the CJP's legal team." CJP reposted that and added "Please note." Bar & Bench and LiveLaw report that Bharti has sought to withdraw the plea. Ratna Singh posted at 1:03 AM: "Since morning no one knows where they are, their families don't have any idea, the lawyers have no clue."

detainees.status: Free — acting as CJP's lawyer at the 11 Oct production; earlier detention reports unconfirmed. ANI reported she was released (~5:53 PM), and Saket court dismissed her plea for an FIR and a release direction (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench, ANI, 5:53 PM). The Hindu live blog (8:13 PM entry) says she posted at 7:13 PM: 'I am still detained. Since 9AM. There are 30 police official for one woman.' The Hindu (8:32 PM) and The Wire (8:54 PM) report a Delhi court dismissed her plea alleging wrongful confinement by police outside her Jangpura home. The Wire quotes her: 'Judge Serving Master' and 'Welcome to new India, where Sarkar can put 30 police personnel confining you...' LiveLaw (9:26 PM): a Delhi court rejected her plea for an FIR against policemen for wrongful confinement and for restraining her from protesting. Neha Bora (AISA) posted at 9:14 PM, 'Why is @whattalawyer still under house arrest?' Attributed as Bora's claim. Status remains conflicting reports as of 10:05 PM. A habeas corpus plea filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity referred to her detention. She posted at 12:48 AM that the petition was not filed by CJP, that CJP is not approaching the Supreme Court, and that CJP's legal team did not approve it. Bharti has sought to withdraw it (Bar & Bench, LiveLaw). She was posting on X between 12:48 AM and 1:46 AM. No outlet has reported her detention status. At 8:02 AM she posted that she will be at Delhi Cantt Police Station at 9 AM, as CJP's legal head, with other advocates, for the production of Dipke, Ranka and Das before an Executive Magistrate. That is consistent with her being free to attend, but no outlet has confirmed her release. On the morning of 11 Oct she was at Delhi Cantt Police Station as CJP's legal head. LiveLaw and Bar & Bench cited her for the Executive Magistrate's release order. No outlet has published a separate confirmation of when her own detention ended. As of 10:05 AM.

timeline.e: INDIA bloc, student unions and other groups begin protests in Delhi against the CEC over SIR.
Rahul Gandhi climbs barricades and leads an 8-hour sit-in at Akashvani Bhawan. About 250 detained, including MPs; all released around 10 PM.
Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi detained a second time near Jantar Mantar. Derek O'Brien and about 90 others also detained.
Dhruv Rathee joins CJP protest in Bengaluru. CJP spokesperson Deepak Baliyan detained in Alwar and released that night.

Supreme Court says there can be no 'complete prohibition' on metro and trains. Delhi HC refuses an urgent hearing for Youth Congress. Delhi Police confirms the protest is denied. Home Secretary tells state police chiefs to stop 'unauthorised entry' into Delhi. INDIA bloc meets the President.
DMRC shuts entry/exit at 45 metro stations until 6 PM on 10 Oct.
Dhruv Rathee detained at his Gurugram home.

image.alt: Dhruv Rathee speaking into a microphone.

timeline.e: Detentions begin at Jantar Mantar. People are put on buses, and stadiums are used as detention centres.
Delhi Police statement: about 500 detained, plus about 50 'with criminal backgrounds'. The district is split into 20 zones, each with its own detention centre.
Dipke, Das and Ranka detained on board their Air India flight at IGI. CJP releases a pre-recorded video handing the lead to Ajinkya Shinde.

image.alt: Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka seated in a police bus.

timeline.e: Lawyers marching from the Supreme Court are detained. A contempt plea is filed in the SC over the metro closures.
Pinarayi Vijayan, John Brittas and K.N. Balagopal detained. Tushar Gandhi detained in Mumbai. CPI(M) says 500+ cadres held at HKS Bhawan. About 200 detained at Connaught Place.
Officials say 25–30 protesters jumped barricades on Imtiaz Ali Marg and threw stones; 2 police personnel injured (PTI, citing officials).
CJI Surya Kant and SG Tushar Mehta speak to authorities, and the detained lawyers are released. Hundreds detained outside Bangla Sahib gurdwara.
Ratna Singh moves Saket court. Neha Bora and Yogendra Yadav detained on the Dilli Haat march. Mamata Banerjee and 5 TMC leaders detained outside her residence.

CPI(M) says former Tripura CM Manik Sarkar and CITU's Elamaram Kareem are held at Bawana stadium. At Saket court, LiveLaw says staff told reporters the magistrate was dictating an order in a different case; Ratna Singh's FIR plea was still pending as of 5:27 PM; the court dismissed it at 5:53 PM.
Manish Sisodia and Punjab AAP leaders Baltej Punia and Sonia Mann detained by Chandigarh Police near the Punjab Chief Electoral Officer's office. Punjab FM Harpal Singh Cheema also took part.

image.alt: A crowd at an outdoor protest, many people holding flags.

timeline.e: Arvind Kejriwal detained by Delhi Police while trying to march to Jantar Mantar. TOI says outside his residence; Business Today says outside Lodhi Estate. Gopal Rai also detained. AAP's Atishi alleges Kejriwal was 'brutally taken into custody'.

image.alt: Arvind Kejriwal standing beside a police bus.

timeline.e: CJP's Ajinkya Shinde, in a video, tells people to march on: 'Wherever the Delhi Police try to stop you, make it your Jantar Mantar.' Says the movement continues till the CEC resigns.
More than 50 protesters detained near Dilli Haat at Neha Bora's call; some say they weren't part of the protest.
About 200 students from Punjab reached the Jantar Mantar area after spending the night at Gurdwara Bangla Sahib; several were detained.
PTI, citing police sources, says Delhi Police detained around 1,000 protesters across the city during the anti-CEC stir.

Dipke's father Bhagwan Dipke questions the heavy deployment: 'It is an agitation of students. Have dacoits from Chambal gathered in Delhi?' and says every Indian has a legal right to protest. His mother Anita Dipke asks why he had to be detained from a flight.

Police sources (PTI) say Delhi Police told Abhijeet Dipke of his grandmother's death and left it to him whether to stay in detention and continue the protest or go home for her last rites. Grandmother Savitribai Shankarrao Dipke, 85, died around 11:30 AM in Santuk Pimpri, Hingoli district, Maharashtra; last rites at 10 AM Sunday 11 Oct (family sources).
After his detention, Kejriwal posts a video on X: 'We have been detained by the police... The youth of the country has awakened. We are not going to be intimidated by Modi's tyranny.'

Sanjay Singh, Saurabh Bharadwaj and Durgesh Pathak detained by Delhi Police along with Arvind Kejriwal. Exact time of detention not given; Tribune logged it at 4:18 PM IST. Place in Delhi not specified.
Kejriwal after detention (PTI video): 'Turn the entire country into Jantar Mantar.'
The Hindu reports CJP activists protesting at Chennai's Elliot's Beach; police detained several after a verbal spat.
Mamata Banerjee begins a dharna at Dwarka Sector 17 police station, where she is detained (Derek O'Brien, via Deccan Herald reporter Shemin Joy). Reporter post on X, not yet in a published article.
NDTV: Chennai Police detained 100+ protesters near Elliott's Beach demanding the CEC's resignation; activist Radhika Ganesh among those detained.
NDTV visuals: security forces including Delhi Police and RAF detain protesters at Connaught Place Outer Circle who tried to march past barricades.

Prashant Bhushan (senior advocate) and Dipankar Bhattacharya (CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary) detained near INA Market with Neha Bora (AISA president) and Yogendra Yadav. Exact detention time not given. The Sentinel calls Bora an AAP leader; Deccan Herald and earlier reports say AISA president.

Mamata Banerjee will stay in Delhi for an INDIA bloc march to the Supreme Court on Monday 12 Oct instead of returning to Kolkata; Abhishek Banerjee will also come back for it (Deccan Herald reporter Shemin Joy). Reporter post on X, not yet in a published article.

Delhi Police officials (via ANI): Dipke was detained because the protest call was not permitted; he was told of his grandmother's death 'with due sensitivity', told the funeral time, and offered possible facilitation for his journey to his hometown on humanitarian grounds.

Scroll: a protester detained in Pune says 'We were dragged on the city streets. Multiple women have sustained bruises.' Unverified individual claim on social media; no detention count given. Scroll also reports its journalist Divya Aslesha was detained in Pune.

BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad: 'CJP is doing shadow boxing for the Aam Aadmi Party'; calls the opposition 'defeated, desperate individuals ... weaponizing street protests'; defends SIR as a legal provision conducted 'more than nine times'.
Bengaluru: at least 50 AISA students detained at Freedom Park (The Hindu, 3:21 PM).

AISA's claim: police illegally took the phones of Neha Bora (AISA president) and AISA activist Nirma at the Maidan Garhi detention centre, kept them in an isolated room, and are not letting lawyers meet them (The Hindu, 4:09 PM).
Priyanka Gandhi Vadra: 'India is not a democracy anymore. It is a dictatorship being run by Modi and Shah' (The Hindu).
CJP, SFI and AISF representatives to address a press meet on 'Jantar Mantar 2.0' at HKS Surjeet Bhawan at 5 PM (The Hindu, 4:34 PM).

Yogendra Yadav, in a video shared by The Wire (recorded earlier): 'Protesters succeeded in setting up Jantar Mantar 2.0 at several sites in Delhi.' The video does not indicate that he has been released.
NDTV: BJP attacks Congress and CJP — 'India Is Not A Banana Republic'.
Mumbai: police clash with protesters near August Kranti Marg; protesters detained at August Kranti Maidan (The Hindu). No detention count given.
Scroll: nearly 5,000 protesters detained in Delhi, citing The Hindu.
Sonam Wangchuk says India is in 'a state of undeclared emergency' and he will be compelled to consider an anshan (fast) or padyatra if detained protesters are not released by tomorrow (The Hindu).

CJP says it still has no information on Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka's whereabouts and is concerned for their safety. At 1:08 PM, intelligence sources told The Hindu the three were taken to three different locations in Delhi-NCR. No release reported.
Indian Youth Congress launches a legal helpline (9582223884) for people detained or threatened over the protests (PTI via Tribune).

Hindustan Times: INDIA bloc to hold a mega protest in Delhi on Monday 12 Oct. Mamata Banerjee cancelled her return to Kolkata to join; Abhishek Banerjee will travel back to Delhi for it. This confirms the earlier Deccan Herald reporter post.
The Hindu: a group of individuals threatened, chased and assaulted some protesters in Connaught Place. Perpetrators not identified.
SFI says students and public intellectuals will hold a press conference at HKS Surjeet Bhawan at 5 PM. No reports yet of what was said.

Saket court: the CJM's order on Ratna Singh's FIR plea was under dictation at about 4:58 PM. The court said it would decide on the application as filed, not on changed circumstances (Bar & Bench, LawBeat). The plea was later dismissed at 5:53 PM.
Officials told PTI that Delhi Police detained over 3,000 people during the anti-CEC protest. The Hindu's summary says 3,300; The Tribune says 3,000.
CPI(M) calls on all party units to protest against the day's police repression, the CEC and SIR (The Wire).
Rahul Gandhi releases a video on X telling the youth: 'Keep protesting. We are proud of you' (The Hindu live blog).
SFI leader Aishe Ghosh posts a video alleging police abuse during detention and saying 'Jantar Mantar 2.0 is on' (The Hindu live blog). Attributed as her allegation.
SFI alleges people 'dressed as Delhi police' who attacked protesters and assaulted women students were not wearing name tags (The Hindu live blog). Attributed as SFI's allegation.
TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee (ANI) says about 2,500 people were detained across Delhi.
Hindustan Times: CJP renews its call — 'Wherever Delhi Police stop you, make your own Jantar Mantar'.
PTI, citing officials: police detained around 200 people at Mumbai's August Kranti Maidan. The Hindu (5:19 PM) reports a police clash with protesters there.

Police account (ANI): a police officer was injured after stone pelting during the protest. The officer says a crowd of 100–150 had gathered on the road near the Hanuman temple and protesters twisted his arm while being detained.

The Hindu: hundreds of CJP volunteers and other citizens brought from multiple places across Delhi are being held at Chhatrasal Stadium, Model Town, used as a makeshift holding centre (live blog 4:54 PM entry by Vijaita Singh).

CJP's appeal: it publicly asked Delhi Police to release Abhijeet Dipke immediately, saying his whereabouts are still unknown, his lawyers cannot reach him, and his family cannot tell him of his grandmother's death. This is CJP's claim, and it conflicts with earlier police sources who said he had been informed.
PTI video: police stop protesters marching towards Jantar Mantar on Safdarjung flyover.
NDTV: Delhi Police shares a video explaining why permission for the CJP protest was denied.
Scroll: hundreds raise slogans against CEC Gyanesh Kumar on Aurobindo Marg, South Delhi; police try to break up the crowd using force.

Kerala CM V.D. Satheesan (via UNI) says Pinarayi Vijayan is held at Mandir Marg police station, and that Kerala's Chief Secretary and Resident Commissioner are in contact with Delhi Police to coordinate his immediate release. No release reported.
PTI: 124 former IAS/IFS officers issue an open letter defending the Election Commission and SIR.
ThePrint: around 3,500 people detained in Delhi. Police say the detentions could last up to 24 hours.

Actor Imran Khan detained by Mumbai Police at August Kranti Maidan, the proposed Mumbai venue backing CJP's call. He told IANS he is not part of any organisation and does not speak as a representative.
ThePrint ground report: mini protests spring up at detention centres and on Delhi roads, with people saying they will create their own Jantar Mantar.

The Hindu, citing a senior officer: two Delhi Police personnel, Suman (Pink Force) and Dheeraj Yadav, were injured during the detention of around 1,000 protesters in New Delhi district. Circumstances are being ascertained. Police account.

ANI: Mamata Banerjee alleges Delhi Police 'kidnapped' her and is holding a protest at Dwarka North police station. An earlier reporter post had placed her at Dwarka Sector 17; both accounts are kept, attributed. TMC MLA Kunal Ghosh condemned her detention (IANS, 5:35 PM).
Mumbai Police, via ANI: over 400 people detained so far at August Kranti Maidan. PTI had reported about 200 at 5:18 PM.
CJP's claim: its national spokesperson Siddhant Bharadwaj and his team were detained. Place not stated. Attributed to CJP.
ThePrint ground report: police and RAF detain protesters at Connaught Place, including people who came from Assam and Chhattisgarh.
Police account (ANI): Sub-Inspector Bajrang Yadav says he was injured while stopping people running from the direction of the CPM office.

The Hindu: what happened moments before Dipke, Das and Ranka were detained aboard Air India flight AI 2428. The detention caught even the airline by surprise and raises questions about police access to the aircraft.
DMK chief M.K. Stalin says the BJP government detained former chief ministers Pinarayi Vijayan, Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee and Manik Sarkar, plus M.A. Baby and student leaders (The Hindu).
The Wire: some buses Delhi Police is using to detain protesters are marked 'election duty'.

Saket court dismissed Ratna Singh's plea for an FIR against police over her detention and for a direction to release her (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench, ANI). ANI reported she had been released. The Hindu later said she posted at 7:13 PM that she was still detained. The reports conflict.
Scroll: reporter Divya Aslesha recounts being detained by Pune Police and taken to Lashkar police station. She says a senior officer told her she was detained 'by mistake'.
CPI(ML) holds a road protest in Vannarpettai, Tirunelveli, against the CEC (The Hindu live blog).
Congress MP Pawan Khera (IANS): 'Today, they didn't spare lawyers, they didn't spare journalists... This is an emergency!' Attributed as his statement.

Bengaluru Police Commissioner Seemant Singh: permission was only for the protest, not a march to the CEO's office, so marchers were taken into preventive detention (The Hindu live blog). Police account.

Indian Express live: Rahul Gandhi visited Rashtrapati Bhavan with other Opposition leaders. Exact visit time not given. BJP MP Sambit Patra called him a 'nalayak neta' and accused him of trying to draw the President into a street protest. Both statements attributed.
ThePrint: in a Rohtak village, villagers detained policemen who had come to detain a protester.

Tushar Gandhi is still held at DN Nagar police station, Mumbai. Aaditya Thackeray and MP Sanjay Raut were at the station with party workers demanding his release (IANS, The Hindu, 5:50–6:15 PM). Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Haroon Khan says Gandhi was detained in Bandra and brought there.
DMRC: the 45 Metro stations closed since 9 PM Friday will stay closed till 10 PM tonight (10 Oct). Security agencies will review after that (ANI, PTI).
LiveLaw posts a video it says shows a male CRPF officer manhandling a woman advocate near Mandi House, Delhi. Attributed to LiveLaw's video.

Delhi CM Rekha Gupta (PTI): 'Delhi will not be held hostage.' She calls CJP the 'B-Team' of Rahul Gandhi and Arvind Kejriwal and says the 'politics of spreading anarchy under guise of democracy' will be fought. Attributed as her statement.

Mamata Banerjee, still held, tells PTI she has been in a prison van for about two hours: 'We obeyed and accepted whatever they said. Despite that, they picked us up... I have never used this prison van; it is meant for criminals.' Attributed as her statement. Earlier, ~6:01 PM, she said she will join the INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court on Monday. The Hindu live blog also says CJP, SFI and AISF began a joint press conference in New Delhi.
The Wire: PhD student Mohd Alfauz spent 22 hours in police detention ahead of the 10 Oct protest and describes 'moral lectures, intimidation'. Attributed to his account via The Wire.
PTI video: AAP workers clash with police during a protest in Chandigarh.
Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Varun Sardesai detained by Mumbai Police during the anti-CEC protest (The Hindu live blog, 6:21 PM). Held at last report.
A rally near Sundarayya Vignana Kendram, Hyderabad, demands that SIR be scrapped and the CEC resign (The Hindu).

Rahul Gandhi (The Wire): 'Arrest All the Leaders. Arrest All the Young People. Arrest Us All.' Attributed as his statement. Union Minister Piyush Goyal responded that Rahul 'has no respect for any constitutional authority' (IANS, 6:23 PM).
INDIA bloc and student groups hold a rally in Visakhapatnam (The Hindu live blog).
A torchlight march in Nashik against the CEC and SIR (IANS).
Police detain a large number of CJP workers at the INA flyover, Delhi (IANS).
AIUDF president Badruddin Ajmal backs the protest and the demand for Gyanesh Kumar's resignation (ANI).
Journalists' bodies condemn the crackdown as an 'assault on press freedom'. The Wire says several journalists were detained despite showing press cards.
Union Minister Ramdas Athawale (ANI): police did not oppose an earlier CJP protest while it was peaceful, but violence and stone-pelting at police followed. Attributed as his statement.
The Wire: women protesters gathered outside Gurudwara Bangla Sahib, and several protesters who had taken shelter inside the gurdwara were detained.

Bar & Bench video: Delhi Police carry Senior Advocate Shadan Farasat away by his arms and legs, his shirt torn, during a detention earlier today. He was later released, and told Bar & Bench he had intervened to stop police manhandling. LiveLaw also posted the detention video (6:46 PM).

Delhi Police have started releasing protesters. A senior officer told The Hindu: 'We have initiated the process to release protesters, who were detained across Delhi during the protest.' The Hindu says over 5,000 were detained, including Abhijeet Dipke, CPI(M) leaders and student activists. No named leader's release was confirmed.
Mumbai: protesters forcibly detained near August Kranti Maidan (The Hindu video).

ANI describes West Bengal ministers Tapas Roy and Bishal Lama criticising the CJP protest. Roy called protesters 'traitors' and 'anti-national'. Lama said they should approach the court. Attributed as their statements.

Sources told The Wire that Trolley Times editor Navkiran and about 20 other women were detained after dark in Delhi. They are in a bus with police who have no name tags and do not know where they are being taken.

AAP workers gherao Jaffarpur Kalan police station in Dwarka, saying Arvind Kejriwal, Sanjay Singh, Anurag Dhanda (AAP national media in-charge) and Saurabh Bharadwaj are held there (PTI video). Attributed as the AAP workers' account. Kejriwal and the AAP leaders are still held; no release reported.
CJP protest leader Ajinkya Shinde (TOI): 'Wherever they stop you, that becomes Jantar Mantar.' He urges supporters to stay peaceful.

Sonam Wangchuk warns of another fast unless detainees are released (Indian Express). Hindustan Times also reports the warning. The Hindu had said he would consider an anshan or padyatra if they are not released by tomorrow.
The Wire: students detained at Bawana police station were denied drinking water.

Pinarayi Vijayan released. In a PTI video after his release, the former Kerala chief minister accuses Delhi Police of behaviour unbecoming of a police force and says he is proud to have been part of the protest. IANS later confirmed (9:20 PM) that Brittas and Balagopal were released with him from Mandir Marg police station.
The Wire: women were released from Maidan Garhi police station, and AISA president Neha Bora got her phone back. The Wire does not say Neha Bora herself was released. Her release is not confirmed.

Delhi Police, via IANS, rebut social-media claims: Dipke's grandmother's death was promptly conveyed to him with due sensitivity, he was told the funeral time, and he was offered all possible assistance to travel home on humanitarian grounds. NDTV (7:41 PM) says that by evening it was not clear whether he would be released. Attributed as the police account.
NDTV video: a clash during the CJP protest in Delhi, with police personnel injured.
CJP press conference: members say they still have no information on the whereabouts of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka (The Hindu live blog).

Delhi Police sources (The Hindu): women protesters and senior citizens are being released from detention centres first, and due legal process will be followed in the case of CJP leaders. Deployment will continue amid expectations of another protest call by CJP, AIYF, AISF and SFI. NDTV (7:41 PM) adds that the heavy deployment will continue on Sunday. Attributed as the police account.

Arvind Kejriwal, in his own video (via IANS; Hindustan Times at 7:57 PM), says he and others were brought to Jafarpur police station and that several hundred people surround it with only 15–20 police: 'this place is also gradually turning into another Jantar Mantar.' Still held. This matches the earlier AAP account of Jaffarpur Kalan police station.

NDTV, with PTI inputs: over 1,500 people were detained across Delhi, including four former chief ministers — Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar. Detainees were held in large stadiums and many were released later in the evening. Mamata wore a band-aid over her mouth and called it 'a Super Emergency'. The INDIA bloc has called a protest on Monday, and its leaders will meet CJI Surya Kant on Monday to submit a memorandum (Rahul Gandhi).

The Supreme Court will hold a special sitting on Sunday 11 Oct on advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi's contempt plea over the blanket closure of metro stations and train cancellations, alleged to violate the court's 9 Oct order. Bench: Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana. IANS (7:57 PM) names the respondents as Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and DMRC chairperson D. Thara.

Senior advocate and TMC Rajya Sabha MP Menaka Guruswamy has moved the Supreme Court against the preventive detention of opposition leaders, including four former chief ministers, during today's Delhi protests. The plea is listed before the same special Sunday bench (Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana) on 11 Oct. She told Bar & Bench that preventive detention cannot be used to suppress the right to peaceful protest.
The Tribune: Ajinkya Shinde, CJP organisation in-charge from Latur, has taken command of the protest after Dipke picked him to lead it.
ThePrint ground report: police and RAF detain protesters at Connaught Place as the chaos intensifies, including people who came from Assam and Chhattisgarh.

Mamata Banerjee released from Delhi Police detention (ANI video, ~8:09 PM). PTI (8:17 PM), after her release: 'Right now we won't say anything because tomorrow the INDIA Alliance has called for a united stand...' Release of the other TMC leaders with her was not separately confirmed.

The Delhi High Court Bar Association strongly condemns the 'illegal detention' of several advocates and 'disproportionate' force against lawyers, including senior advocates. It calls for an impartial inquiry and accountability (Bar & Bench, LiveLaw, 8:11–8:24 PM).

The Hindu: Ratna Singh posted at 7:13 PM, 'I am still detained. Since 9AM. There are 30 police official for one woman.' This conflicts with ANI's earlier report that she had been released at about 5:53 PM. The Hindu (8:32 PM) and The Wire (8:54 PM) say a Delhi court dismissed her wrongful-confinement plea.
Arvind Kejriwal released from Jaffarpur (Jafarpur Kalan) police station (PTI video, ~8:13 PM). Release of Sanjay Singh, Saurabh Bharadwaj and Durgesh Pathak was not separately confirmed.
Scroll: police reportedly detained more than 7,000 protesters in Delhi today, with smaller protests in Mumbai, Pune and Bengaluru. Attributed to Scroll.
Police say the Jantar Mantar area remained clear of protesters. The New Delhi DCP shared a video to counter social-media claims of a large gathering there (The Hindu).
Indian Express: 245 trains cancelled, including Rajdhani and Shatabdi services.
NDTV: actor Imran Khan and his relative Zayn Marie Khan were detained at the CJP protest at August Kranti Maidan, Mumbai. She shared a video from inside the police van.

Menaka Guruswamy's Supreme Court plea is a habeas corpus petition. It challenges the detention of Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar, and other political leaders. It is to be heard on Sunday 11 Oct at the special sitting before Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana (LiveLaw). Bar & Bench says the special Sunday sitting will hear pleas against the detention of opposition leaders.

Neha Bora, AISA national president, and the other women detained with her were released from Maidan Garhi police station (India Today, ~8:30 PM). This supersedes the earlier report that her own release was not confirmed. Yogendra Yadav later wrote at 9:35 PM that he had been released from Maidangarhi police station. Prashant Bhushan and Dipankar Bhattacharya still have no individual release report.

SFI joint secretary Aishe Ghosh demanded the release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka (The Hindu live blog). The Hindu (8:55 PM) confirms Aishe Ghosh and Neha Bora were detained earlier in the day.

UN Human Rights said it was concerned by reports of mass detentions of demonstrators, protest leaders, members of civil society organisations, lawyers and journalists, before and during the day's demonstrations in Delhi, and called on authorities to ensure the right to peaceful assembly is fully respected and fulfilled (via The Hindu live blog).
Pune: police detained about 80–100 CJP protesters at Lal Mahal Chowk, where there was no police permission, and took them to Lashkar police station (IANS).
The Wire quotes Ratna Singh on the court order that dismissed her plea: 'Judge Serving Master' and 'Welcome to new India, where Sarkar can put 30 police personnel confining you...'

CJP's Ajinkya Shinde, at a joint press conference with SFI and AISF: 'We will come back tomorrow and walk towards Jantar Mantar again.' The protest will continue until Gyanesh Kumar resigns. He alleged police did not let Dipke speak to his lawyer or family after news of his grandmother's death. CJP says Dipke, Das and Ranka were taken to different locations across Delhi-NCR (The Hindu; IANS video).
IANS: Pinarayi Vijayan, CPI(M) MP John Brittas and former Kerala minister K.N. Balagopal were released from Mandir Marg police station.

Indian Express: hundreds of people were detained at Nana Chowk, near August Kranti Maidan in Mumbai, at a gathering called by Tushar Gandhi in support of CJP. Existing counts still range from about 200 (NDTV/PTI) to over 400 (Mumbai Police via ANI).
The Hindu video: BSF personnel carried Beretta MX4 submachine guns and INSAS rifles near Jantar Mantar.

Yogendra Yadav says he has been released. In his own post he wrote that he had just been released from Maidangarhi police station and was reaching Sanjay Colony police station. No other outlet had confirmed it yet. Release of Prashant Bhushan and Dipankar Bhattacharya was still not reported.

Delhi Police sources (ANI): all the detainees have been released from the detention centres except CJP leaders, and due legal process will be followed for the CJP leaders. Earlier, at 9:18 PM, police sources told IANS that most of those detained today had been released.
CPI(M): SFI general secretary Srijan Bhattacharya briefed the media at HKS Surjeet Bhawan on the next steps, with CJP, AISF and other student groups. The line was 'Not an inch back'.

CJP and student groups say they will march to Jantar Mantar every day until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns or is removed (NDTV). The Hindu (9:51 PM): CJP has called a march to Jantar Mantar again on Sunday 11 Oct. NDTV says police said heavy security will continue.
NDTV: a BJP leader's daughter was detained during the Delhi protests. She said she had been sitting in a park.
NDTV: the INDIA bloc will hold a mega protest against Gyanesh Kumar on Monday 12 Oct. Rahul Gandhi has already said INDIA bloc leaders will meet CJI Surya Kant on Monday to submit a memorandum.
PTI video: Aligarh Muslim University students were detained in Delhi during the protest. Third-party video.

Scroll: about 150 protesters picked up from Gurudwara Bangla Sahib around 3 PM were taken to Chhatrasal Stadium in north Delhi and kept about five hours. One detainee told Scroll they have now been released.

NDTV: all of about 3,000 detainees were released except Abhijeet Dipke, Dhruv Rathee and two other CJP leaders. The report says Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Dhruv Rathee remained in custody. Police had said Dipke was told he could leave for his grandmother's funeral, but by evening it was not clear if he would be released.

image.alt: Police officers carrying batons move through a crowd.

timeline.e: The Supreme Court special Sunday sitting is still on. LiveLaw says the court will hear on Sunday 11 Oct the contempt petition alleging that metro shutdowns and train cancellations violated the court's 9 Oct order. The Hindu also noted the listing at 9:17 PM.
Arvind Kejriwal (his own post) asked the Prime Minister where Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, Dhruv Rathee and Saurav Das are being held.
The Hindu: Air India has sought official clarification after police boarded flight AI 2428 and detained Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka from their seats on landing.

The Lawyers' Association for Constitution wrote to the Delhi Police Commissioner alleging Supreme Court advocate Fidal Tom, who appeared with Kapil Sibal in the Supreme Court on Friday on the Delhi shutdown, was assaulted by police and is illegally detained at Sanjay Colony police station. The association seeks his release and medical treatment (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench). Allegation, not a police finding.
The Hindu: with central Delhi fortified, many groups protested away from Jantar Mantar after learning leaders were detained.
All Delhi Metro station gates reopened and interchanges were restored (DMRC via IANS). Delhi Police reposted DMRC at 11:09 PM. 45 stations had been closed.

PTI (10:38 PM): CJP calls a protest at Jantar Mantar on Sunday at 10 AM, and Delhi Police has issued a traffic advisory. PTI (10:31 PM): CJP says the protest will continue across the country until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns. IANS (10:46 PM): CJP national organisation in-charge Ajinkya Shinde says they will return to Jantar Mantar tomorrow; heavy police deployment remains.

NCP(SP) MP Supriya Sule, in a post reposted by CJP: "Deeply concerned by reports that Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka remain in custody, with no warrant shown." TMC MP Derek O'Brien (CJP repost, 10:44 PM): "WHERE IS ABHIJEET? 11 hours and counting."

Hindustan Times: Delhi Police posted on X that Abhijeet Dipke was "immediately" told of his grandmother's death and the funeral time and offered "possible facilitation" to travel home on humanitarian grounds. CJP replied: "Where is Abhijeet? His family wants to talk to him... last rites tomorrow morning." The same report says police say nearly 4,000 people were detained in Delhi today.

Yogendra Yadav (his own posts) says he is staying at Sanjay Colony police post over four colleagues he alleges were "brutally beaten", including an 18-year-old and a lawyer. He says lawyers were not allowed to meet them, demands immediate medical exams (MLC), and says he will not leave until they are released. His claim. He had written at 9:35 PM that he was released from Maidangarhi police station; this is not a new detention of Yadav.

CJP: "It's been 12 hours. No information. No accountability." It demands the immediate release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, disclosure of their whereabouts, and access to lawyers. They remain detained.

LiveLaw: Senior Advocate Dinesh Dwivedi was detained by Delhi Police today. He said he was "simply standing there" and "Do you think what is happening in Delhi is lawful? It is rubbish." No release reported.
Congress leader Bhupesh Baghel (ANI, Raipur) criticises Delhi Police treatment of Rahul Gandhi and the protesters.
Congress leader Udit Raj (IANS): the protest was not CJP alone; SFI, AISA and TMC were involved, and "AAP was leading it" (his claim).
Odisha Congress chief Bhakta Charan Das (ANI): protesters in Delhi were peaceful.

An account named Cockroaches of India (@CJP_for_India), which is not the official CJP handle @Cockroachisback, asked everyone to reach Jantar Mantar by 10 AM. Treat this as unverified. The Sunday 10 AM march itself was already reported by PTI.
India Today: lawyers detained at Yamuna Sports Complex were seen singing the national anthem, in a video shared by Congress.
DCP New Delhi (ANI) responded to a video of police wearing shoes inside Gurudwara Bangla Sahib, saying the staff were walking in a common passage. Attributed as the police's explanation.
Hindustan Times: 124 former bureaucrats defended the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision.
IANS: Mumbai's Gamdevi police registered a case against Tushar Gandhi, actor Imran Khan, Ali Bhojani and 300–400 others under BNS sections 223, 126(2) and 189 for protesting without permission.

Hindustan Times: Delhi Police posted a video on X, "Broken promises, shattered trust", explaining why they denied permission for the Jantar Mantar protest. Police say CJP broke the signed undertaking it gave during the June–July protests against then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Attributed as the police's claim. The same report says Dipke, Das, Ranka and Dhruv Rathee are still held and everyone else was released.
IANS: CJP's Ajinkya Shinde wrote to the Delhi Police Commissioner asking where Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka are.

India Today: the INDIA bloc march in Delhi on Monday 12 Oct demands Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. PTI (12:39 AM) restates the Monday 12 Oct march against CEC Gyanesh Kumar on 'vote chori', and says a senior delegation will submit a memorandum to the Chief Justice seeking intervention.

India rejected the UN Human Rights Office's concerns as "misplaced" and an "unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of India", in a statement on the India at UN account. "India is the world's largest democracy, where the right to peaceful assembly is guaranteed by our Constitution." It also said the office "would also do well to devote comparable attention to large-scale protests elsewhere" (NDTV, Hindustan Times, IANS).

image.alt: Security personnel at barricades on Jantar Mantar Road at night

timeline.e: KC Venugopal (ANI) says the INDIA bloc will give a memorandum to the Chief Justice on Monday.

A habeas corpus petition was filed in the Supreme Court by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity (about 11:39 PM to 12:10 AM), not by CJP. It seeks production and release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka and others, their whereabouts, the legal grounds for each detention, and preservation of CCTV, police diaries and movement registers. It asks whether the Section 163 BNSS order for Parliament Street can justify detentions at the airport and in Gurugram, and it asks for the custodial status of Ratna Singh and other advocates. It says it does not seek immunity from lawful action for any separate offence. LawBeat says the plea also names Dhruv Rathee; Bar & Bench's report does not (single source). Correction: CJP later said it did not file or approve the plea, and Bharti sought to withdraw it (see 12:48 AM).

image.alt: Man in a Cockroach Janta Party T-shirt at a protest

timeline.e: The same unofficial account, @CJP_for_India (not the official CJP handle @Cockroachisback), posted at 12:11 AM, quoting Neha Bora: "Another part of Delhi will become Jantar Mantar tomorrow! Stay tuned for updates." Treat this as unverified.

NDTV: Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Dhruv Rathee remained in custody as of 12:15 AM. The report says at least 3,000 people were detained in Delhi and that all others were released. NDTV says police told Dipke he could leave for his grandmother's funeral, but it is unclear whether he will be released. HT (11:25 PM) says the same four are still held. Social claims that Rathee has been released are unverified.

image.alt: Delhi Police personnel outside Block A, Connaught Place, after the anti-CEC protest

timeline.e: PTI restates that the INDIA bloc will hold a protest march in Delhi on Monday 12 Oct against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on 'vote chori', and that a senior delegation will submit a memorandum to the Chief Justice seeking intervention.

Correction: the Supreme Court habeas corpus plea for Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and others was filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity, not by CJP. CJP says it did not file it. At 12:48 AM, CJP legal cell chief Ratna Singh posted: "This petition is not filed by @Cockroachisback. We are not approaching the Supreme Court, and no habeas corpus petition has been approved by the CJP's legal team." CJP reposted that and added "Please note" (12:50–12:52 AM). Bar & Bench (12:46 AM and 12:58 AM) and LiveLaw (12:57 AM) report that Bharti has sought to withdraw the plea. Menaka Guruswamy's own habeas plea is a separate case and is unaffected.

PTI: four journalists' organisations, including the Press Club of India and the Indian Women's Press Corps, condemned the detention and harassment of several journalists covering the Delhi protests and demanded an apology and an inquiry.

The Wire: advocate Fidal Tom (spelled Fidel Tom in The Wire) and students Saurabh, Nikhil and Harsh were released by police shortly after midnight from Sanjay Colony police post (Maidan Garhi). A medico-legal examination was conducted. The Wire's account: Tom went to the post to seek the students' release, was detained himself, and was allegedly taken to a washroom and beaten by several police personnel, including a plain-clothes man (an account shared with The Wire and student activists). AISA activist Abhigyan told The Wire all four were beaten badly. The SHO told The Wire he would find out and respond. Maktoob (12:22 AM): AISA alleged Saurabh, its Jamia Millia Islamia secretary, was beaten so badly he could not walk (AISA claim). This updates the earlier report that they were still held.

image.alt: Lawyers gathered outside a police post at night

timeline.e: Yogendra Yadav (his own post) says that at 1 AM, after his colleagues were released, they returned to where the day began. He wrote that they set out to stop Jantar Mantar 2.0 and 22 Jantar Mantars sprang up in Delhi, and that the struggle will continue.

Indian Express: around 30,000 police personnel and 200 companies of paramilitary forces will remain deployed on Sunday, ahead of CJP's 10 AM march to Jantar Mantar. Barricades at Parliament Street and Jantar Mantar stay in place. A police officer said metro and train measures "could be taken depending on the situation". Police will review on Sunday evening before deciding Monday's deployment. AISA's N Sai Balaji alleged some AISA workers were "brutally beaten in detention" and not yet released as of Saturday night (AISA claim). The CJP-SFI-AISF alliance said it would call a protest in the coming days.

image.alt: Security personnel behind chained barricades on Baba Kharak Singh Marg, Saturday

timeline.e: Bar & Bench: the Supreme Court special bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana assembles at 10:30 AM today. Matters: Shailendra Mani Tripathi's contempt plea against Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and DMRC chair D. Thara; Menaka Guruswamy's plea against preventive detention of opposition leaders, including four former chief ministers; and detention and alleged police excesses against lawyers, including Senior Advocate Shadan Farasat. Advocate Aman Prasad's new contempt petition is likely to be mentioned. RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha has also moved the court the same morning.

A new contempt petition in the Supreme Court against Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar was filed by advocate Aman Prasad (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench). He alleges "indiscriminate violence" on 10 Oct: protesters near Jantar Mantar, INA and Dilli Haat assaulted; a protester lifted, thrown down and beaten near INA; a young advocate beaten after intervening when police allegedly pulled at a woman's trousers, with head injuries and a hospital trip in Chhatarpur Enclave; women manhandled by male officers; Scroll's Ayush Tiwari detained despite a press pass; officers without name tags; 45 of 57 metro stations shut. It relies on the court's 28 July, 18 August and 9 Oct orders. Likely to be mentioned at today's 10:30 AM sitting. These are the petitioner's allegations.
ANI video (7:39–7:40 AM) shows heavy security and barricades at Jantar Mantar. PTI video (7:24 AM) shows security beefed up near Janpath.

Police sources, via DNA (8:00 AM): Delhi Police has released over 7,000 people detained during the CJP-led protest, while Abhijeet Dipke and Saurav Das remain in custody. ET Now (~7:19 AM): all 7,000 detainees were released except Dipke, Dhruv Rathee and two others. Indian Express: a CJP statement says more than 15,000 people, including students, civil society members and political leaders, faced detention and police action (CJP claim). Police sources told IE that detainees were kept at around 30 detention centres.

RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha has moved the Supreme Court seeking urgent directions against Delhi Police's alleged illegal detentions, "abduction" and house arrests of "unarmed" protesters, student leaders, advocates, politicians and civilians (LiveLaw). He alleges "disproportionate use of police force" and "sexual harassment of women" protesters, and says the metro shutdown violated court directions. Allegations are his.

CJP legal head Ratna Singh (her own post): "Abhijeet, Ashutosh and Saurav will be produced before the Executive Magistrate at Delhi Cantt Police Station at 9 AM today. A Delhi police official informed me about this in the morning. As CJP's Legal Head, I will be at the police station along with other advocates representing us." This is the first indication of where and when the three will appear. Not yet reported by an outlet. Dhruv Rathee is not mentioned. There is no report yet on whether Dipke can attend his grandmother's funeral at 10 AM in Hingoli.

NDTV: political controversy after opposition leaders alleged police personnel inside Gurudwara Bangla Sahib disrespected the shrine's sanctity. A BJP MP defended the action, saying gurudwaras should not be used for political protests. The post does not name them. Allegation by opposition leaders; the BJP MP's response.
Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal (LiveLaw): "Tired of going to the Supreme Court again and again... I have lost trust."

The account @CJP_for_India, which is not the official CJP handle @Cockroachisback, posted a statement it attributed to Ratna Singh: "This petition is not filed by @CJP_for_India. We are not approaching the Supreme Court, and no habeas corpus petition has been approved by the CJP's legal team." Treat this as unverified. It is not a post from the official CJP account.
LiveLaw: Delhi Police placed Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka under preventive arrest under BNSS Sections 126 and 170. Bar & Bench reported the same at 8:32 AM.

LiveLaw: a CJP member filed a habeas corpus petition in the Supreme Court seeking production and release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and others. CJP's official account has not posted this. A disavowal appeared on @CJP_for_India, which is not the official handle @Cockroachisback, and that post is unverified.
India Today, citing police sources: "No arrests have been made in the case." This was before the reports that Dipke, Das and Ranka had been placed under preventive arrest and then released.
PTI: police confirm that Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were placed under preventive arrest. Indian Express reported the same at 9:34 AM. The sections later cited are BNSS 126 and 170.
PTI: former BJP MP Kirit Somaiya urged Mumbai Police to act against actor Imran Khan for joining a Mumbai protest in support of CJP, and raised his citizenship. Somaiya's demand.
PTI: stringent traffic curbs are in force across Delhi for a second day. India Today (9:25 AM): four pleas over the Delhi shutdown are before the Supreme Court's special bench.

Hindustan Times, citing PTI: the Press Club of India, the Indian Women's Press Corps, the Delhi Union of Journalists and the Kerala Union of Working Journalists (Delhi unit) demand a public apology from Delhi Police. They say journalists from The Quint, The Wire, Scroll, Reporter TV, Navbharat Times and Newslaundry, and senior journalist Paranjoy Guha Thakurta, were detained despite showing press cards, and that some had phones and equipment seized. They called it "reminiscent of a fascist state." HT also reports that men claiming to be from Bajrang Dal threatened journalists near Palika Bazaar at 2:30 PM on Saturday; police chased them away and detained some.

timeline.e: Dhruv Rathee was released at about 3 AM on Sunday and handed over to his family, Hindustan Times and PTI report, citing officials. He had been picked up from Kendriya Vihar, Gurugram Sector 56, around 7:30 AM on Saturday. An unnamed police officer, quoted by PTI, said he can be detained again, or further legal action might be taken, if he tries to go to Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders. This corrects earlier reports, including ETV Bharat (6:48 AM) and ET Now (~7:19 AM), that he was still in custody.

timeline.e: The Hindu (Vijaita Singh): the Union Home Ministry ordered mobile internet suspended within 500 metres of eight makeshift detention centres in Delhi from noon to 10 PM on 10 Oct. The order, dated 9 Oct, was issued by the Union Home Secretary under the Telecommunications Act, 2023, citing public safety and public order. The venues were Chhatrasal Stadium (Model Town), Rajiv Gandhi Stadium (Bawana), Yamuna Sports Complex, Jasola Sports Complex, Community Centre Daulatpur, Community Centre Pandwala Khurd, Jangli Ram Stadium (Nizampur, Kanjhawala) and Surajmal Stadium (Nangloi). The Hindu says around 2,500 protesters were sent to these centres and released later in the day.

timeline.e: LiveLaw: a prohibitory order under Section 163 BNSS is in force on Bhagwan Das Road in front of the Supreme Court. Police barricades warn that force may be used if people do not disperse peacefully. The INDIA bloc has planned a march to the Supreme Court on Monday.

Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were produced before the Special Executive Magistrate, South West District, at Delhi Cantt Police Station (ANI video, 9:51 AM; LiveLaw, 9:35 AM; Bar & Bench, 9:39 AM).

Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released at about 10 AM on an Executive Magistrate's order at Delhi Cantt Police Station. LiveLaw (9:58 AM) reported the order as relayed by CJP legal head Ratna Singh. Bar & Bench (10:00 AM) reported the three released from detention. They had been held under preventive arrest under BNSS Sections 126 and 170. This corrects earlier reports that they were still in custody. His mother, Anita Dipke, later said he was not allowed to attend his grandmother's funeral (PTI, 11:12 AM). As of this check, the Supreme Court special bench at 10:30 AM had not started, and there was no report yet from CJP's 10 AM march.

Bar & Bench: the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association moved the Supreme Court under Article 32 against the 10 Oct police action on lawyers near the court, alleging illegal detention and manhandling, including of women. SCAORA president Devvrat later argued that the internet was shut for 4 km, virtual courts were inaccessible, and lawyers were "lifted." Allegations are SCAORA's.

LiveLaw, citing CJP legal head Ratna Singh: Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released on condition they will not engage in a breach of the peace for one year. PTI (10:54 AM) says they must "maintain peace" for one year. Delhi Police, via ANI (10:56 AM), say the preventive arrest was under BNSS Sections 126 and 170, that all due legal procedures were followed, and that a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was taken. Police account. CJP counsel Soutik Banerjee said at 10:18 AM that all three were released. Indian Express (10:51 AM) says they walked out of Delhi Cantt police station.

The Supreme Court special Sunday sitting began before Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana. LiveLaw: the court restrained the virtual-hearing facility; petitioner-side lawyers said they would not proceed unless video conferencing was allowed; the court sat in Court No. 5. LiveLaw also reported the Solicitor General joining with senior Delhi Police officers and a virtual-hearing Webex meeting at full capacity, so the virtual-hearing position is unclear. ANI (11:06 AM) said the hearing on the detention pleas had commenced. Bar & Bench named Kapil Sibal, Gopal Sankaranarayanan, Menaka Guruswamy, Arundhati Katju, Sanjay Hegde and Anas Tanwir for the petitioners, and SG Tushar Mehta for the respondents. At 11:10 AM Justice Bagchi said the court would either pass an order that day or post the pleas to Monday. On K.K. Venugopal's contempt plea, the court indicated it would be posted to Monday. Sibal said people were picked up from trains and from outside the 4 km radius, and that the internet was suspended. Gopal Sankaranarayanan handed over video stills of action against lawyers, including Shadan Farasat, and flagged the Section 163 order outside the court.

India Today: CJP will hold a press briefing at 2 PM. Hindustan Times later said the press conference was still set for 2 PM. A post on @CJP_for_India at 11:20 AM, which is not the official CJP handle @Cockroachisback, attributed the 2 PM conference to Ashutosh Ranka. That post is unverified.
Indian Express: four right-wing men were arrested over a viral video showing students and women being assaulted.
PTI: security was increased in Connaught Place and police held a flag march. Hindustan Times' e-paper (10:57 AM) says CJP has called a fresh march to Jantar Mantar today.
LiveLaw: a PIL in the Supreme Court seeks scrutiny of the central Delhi internet shutdown.
PTI video: Abhijeet Dipke's mother, Anita Dipke, said, "Have they achieved anything by not allowing him to attend his grandmother's funeral." He did not attend. He was in Delhi until about 10 AM.
India Today: Delhi Police filed 20 FIRs over the 10 Oct protest, for obstructing official work and assaulting police.

CPI(M) MP John Brittas (PTI, ANI): the protest will continue "without a break" whether or not they are allowed into Jantar Mantar. He says he and Kerala's former chief minister were detained on Saturday.

Ashutosh Ranka wrote on X, in Hindi. The Wire's translation: Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar is a "traitor", and Ranka is ready to stay in jail for his entire life to get him removed. His words, after his release.

Hindustan Times: hundreds of people sheltered in Gurdwara Bangla Sahib on Saturday while police waited outside. HT also says AISA president Neha Bora regrouped protesters at Dilli Haat around 1 PM on Saturday before she and others were detained on Sri Aurobindo Marg.

Menaka Guruswamy in the Supreme Court (Bar & Bench): what is at stake is "the suspension of citizens' peacefully exercised constitutional rights." She said the last time the court had to consider such challenges was during the Emergency. Her comparison. Kapil Sibal asked for an interim order against Section 163 orders, detentions and barricades outside the 4 km zone, and said trains that were supposed to run from their origin did not (LiveLaw). K.K. Venugopal (12:01–12:02 PM) said a former junior of his was lifted into a police van, taken nine kilometres away and dropped 11 kilometres away, and could not reach the court, and that police had no badges (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench). Sibal said journalists were being impeded inside and outside. These are the lawyers' accounts.

Hindustan Times: police are keeping central Delhi sealed on Sunday. Jantar Mantar is shut, borders are barricaded, and traffic is diverted at 30 points, while CJP says it will march again. CJP's Ajinkya Shinde: "We will continue our agitation till Gyanesh Kumar resigns." HT estimates about 7,000 people were detained on Saturday. That figure sits alongside the other attributed counts.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta (Bar & Bench): on the habeas pleas, "a statutory regime was followed", and "Most of these people mentioned here were picked up at 2 p.m. and they were released at around 6 o'clock." He also said there was no curtailment of Metro service on 10 Oct and no reduction in the volume of operations, with 4,157 train trips across a 303-station network. An affidavit is to follow. His submissions.

Shiv Sena's Shaina NC (ANI): "No arrest has been made; rather, preventive action has been taken." She said removing the Chief Election Commissioner is a matter for Parliament, not the streets, referring to the INDIA bloc's 12 Oct protest. Her statement. A woman lawyer fainted in the courtroom around 11:54 AM; the Solicitor General attributed it to the air circulation (Bar & Bench).

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told the Supreme Court that 47 Metro stations were closed or restricted, "only 15%" (LiveLaw). Justice Bagchi noted that the authorities first proposed closing 57 and that 45 were closed after the court's 9 Oct order (Bar & Bench; LiveLaw's quote of the closed figure is 47). The bench asked for a map of the stations in the affidavit, and for the state to explain the circumstances, manner and justification of the detentions. On the Section 163 board on Bhagwan Das Road, the Solicitor General said he had just been informed of it. Justice Bagchi said that if people were not aware of the order, that was a good ground to quash it (LiveLaw).

Hindustan Times: Dhruv Rathee wrote, "I was not arrested or detained, I was KIDNAPPED." HT says he gave no undertaking to Gurugram Police. His claim. HT now says he was detained around 9:30 AM on Saturday; its earlier story said about 7:30 AM. The Hindu (10:53 AM) says he was released around 2 AM; HT and PTI, citing officials, say about 3 AM. The official account of a release at about 3 AM is unchanged. Both the release times and the pickup times are kept.

timeline.e: After his release, Abhijeet Dipke wrote: "Modi, as PM, is an embarrassment to India. Never has this country seen a bigger coward and bully." Hindustan Times and The Wire reported the post. His words. HT says the three were detained from their seats on flight AI 2428, which landed at 10:18 AM on Saturday and was moved to remote bay R12.

image.alt: Abhijeet Dipke

timeline.e: The Supreme Court special bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said it will pass an interim order. LiveLaw: the Metro should function normally unless a law-and-order situation arises, the public should have free movement, the internet should be restored, and lawyers should not be impeded in their professional duties. Bar & Bench quotes Justice Bagchi that no advocate should be hindered in discharging their professional duties, and that the Solicitor General's position is that Metro services are already normal unless a public-order situation arises and that the internet is already restored. SG Tushar Mehta said all Metro stations are open today. India Today's headline said barricades should be removed and the internet cannot be shut down. LiveLaw's wording is the more precise account. The full text was not out yet.

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, in Bengaluru (PTI video), criticised the arrests: "We never arrested people unnecessarily." The Wire published an explainer tracking five sets of pleas in the Supreme Court.

Bar & Bench: Justice Joymalya Bagchi began dictating the Supreme Court's interim order. The order records that the special bench assembled on urgent applications alleging violation of the 9 Oct order and illegal detention of a large number of people on 10 Oct. It records Dr Menaka Guruswamy's statement that GTB Nagar and Vishwavidyalaya Metro stations, and others, were completely shut, which she called a deliberate and wilful violation. That is her allegation, as recorded. The state was asked to explain the detentions and to put station-wise Metro details on a map in its affidavit. K.K. Venugopal's contempt plea is likely to be listed on Monday. The full text was still awaited as of 12:05 PM. No CJP march and no new detentions had been reported.

legal_context: Article 22(1): anyone arrested has the right to be told the grounds and to consult a lawyer. Article 22(2): they must be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours.
D.K. Basu guidelines (SC, 1997): arrest memo, informing a relative, and the place of custody must be disclosed.
BNSS Sec 163: prohibitory orders (formerly CrPC 144). BNSS Sec 172: police may detain people who resist lawful directions.
Note: these are general legal standards shown for reference. Whether they were broken in any specific case has not been decided by a court.

courts.court: Supreme Court (CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana)
courts.action: Called the transport notifications 'overreaching' and ruled out complete prohibition of metro and trains ('don't use a hammer to kill a fly'). The SG agreed authorities would reassess. Compliance reports due in 4 days. The court also said that protesting without permission can lead to prosecution.
Refused an urgent hearing on the Youth Congress plea for permission to protest at Jantar Mantar. Listed for Mon 12 Oct.

Contempt petition filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi over the blanket closure of metro stations and train cancellations, alleged to violate the Supreme Court's 9 Oct order. A special Sunday bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana will hear it on 11 Oct. Respondents named by IANS: Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and DMRC chairperson D. Thara. LiveLaw reported again at 10:02 PM, and The Hindu at 9:17 PM, that the special Sunday sitting on 11 Oct is still listed. 11:08 PM: in a PTI video, petitioner Advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi says the authorities "openly violated" the Supreme Court's 9 Oct order; he filed the contempt petition heard at Sunday's special sitting. Bar & Bench (7:15 AM, 11 Oct) says the special Sunday bench assembles at 10:30 AM.
After SCBA, SCAORA and the SG flagged the detentions, CJI Surya Kant spoke to authorities and the detained lawyers were released.
