courts.court: Supreme Court (special Sunday bench, 10:30 AM: Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana)
courts.action: Menaka Guruswamy's plea is a habeas corpus petition. It challenges the detention of Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan, Manik Sarkar and other political leaders. To be heard on Sunday 11 Oct at the special sitting before Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana (LiveLaw). She told Bar & Bench that preventive detention cannot be used to suppress the right to peaceful protest. Bar & Bench (7:15 AM, 11 Oct): the bench assembles at 10:30 AM. Matters: Shailendra Mani Tripathi's contempt plea against Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and DMRC chair D. Thara; Menaka Guruswamy's plea against preventive detention of opposition leaders, including four former chief ministers; and detention and alleged police excesses against lawyers, including Senior Advocate Shadan Farasat. Advocate Aman Prasad's contempt petition against the Delhi Police Commissioner is likely to be mentioned (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench). RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha has also moved the court the same morning seeking urgent directions (LiveLaw). At the hearing, which began about 10:32 AM, LiveLaw reported that the court restrained the virtual-hearing facility and then sat in Court No. 5; the virtual-hearing position was also described as a Webex meeting at full capacity, so that point is unclear. Bar & Bench named Kapil Sibal, Gopal Sankaranarayanan, Menaka Guruswamy, Arundhati Katju, Sanjay Hegde and advocate-on-record Anas Tanwir for the petitioners, and Solicitor General Tushar Mehta for the respondents. On K.K. Venugopal's contempt plea, Justice Bagchi said a similar petition was already before the court and proposed posting it to Monday; Venugopal asked for listing and replies, and the court said it would. At about 11:48 AM the bench said it will pass an interim order: the Metro should run normally unless a law-and-order situation arises, the public should have free movement, the internet should be restored, and lawyers should not be obstructed in their professional duties (LiveLaw). Bar & Bench quotes Justice Bagchi that no advocate should be hindered in discharging their professional duties, and that he summarised the Solicitor General as saying Metro services are normalised unless a public-order situation arises and that the internet is already restored. SG Tushar Mehta said all Metro stations are open today. India Today's live headline said barricades should be removed across Delhi and the internet cannot be shut down. LiveLaw's wording is the more precise account. From 12:03 PM Justice Bagchi was dictating the order (Bar & Bench). It records urgent applications alleging violation of the 9 Oct order and illegal detention on 10 Oct, and Dr Menaka Guruswamy's statement that GTB Nagar and Vishwavidyalaya Metro stations, and others, were completely shut, which she called a deliberate and wilful violation (her allegation, as recorded). The state was asked to explain the circumstances, manner and justification of the detentions and to give station-wise Metro details on a map in its affidavit. The full text was still awaited as of 12:05 PM.

courts.court: Supreme Court (habeas corpus filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity; withdrawal sought)
courts.action: Correction: this habeas corpus petition was filed under Article 32 by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity, between about 11:39 PM and 12:10 AM. It was not filed by CJP, and CJP's legal team did not approve it. It sought production and release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and others, disclosure of their whereabouts and the legal grounds for each detention, and preservation of CCTV footage, police diaries and movement registers. It asked whether the Section 163 BNSS order for Parliament Street can justify detentions at the airport and in Gurugram. It referred to the detention of Ratna Singh and other advocates and asked for their custodial status. It said it does not seek immunity from lawful action for any separate offence. Respondents named were the Centre, the Delhi government, Delhi Police, and Haryana, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh. Filed through advocates-on-record Rajesh G. Inamdar and Shashwat Anand. LawBeat says the plea also names Dhruv Rathee. Bar & Bench's report does not mention him (single source). At 12:48 AM Ratna Singh, CJP's legal cell chief, posted: "This petition is not filed by @Cockroachisback. We are not approaching the Supreme Court, and no habeas corpus petition has been approved by the CJP's legal team." CJP reposted that and added "Please note." Bar & Bench (12:46 AM and 12:58 AM) and LiveLaw (12:57 AM) report that Bharti has sought to withdraw the plea. It is not described as listed with Menaka Guruswamy's separate habeas plea. Her plea is unaffected; no new report on it.

A new contempt petition against Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar was filed by advocate Aman Prasad (LiveLaw, 7:28 AM; Bar & Bench, 7:53 AM). He alleges police used "indiscriminate violence" against citizens on 10 Oct, in violation of Supreme Court principles. The petition says protesters near Jantar Mantar, INA and Dilli Haat were assaulted; a protester was lifted, thrown to the ground and beaten near INA; a young advocate who intervened when police allegedly pulled at a woman's trousers near INA was beaten, suffered head injuries and was taken to a hospital in Chhatarpur Enclave; women were manhandled by male officers; videos purportedly show a woman dragged by her hair in a detention bus and a woman journalist dragged across a road; Scroll's Ayush Tiwari was detained despite showing a press pass; officers were without name tags; and 45 of 57 metro stations were shut, with road blocks and a mobile-internet shutdown. It relies on the court's 28 July and 18 August orders and the 9 Oct order. LiveLaw says it is likely to be mentioned today, on Bar & Bench's 10:30 AM mentioning list. All of these are the petitioner's allegations.

caveats: Correction: an earlier update wrongly described Gaurav Bharti as a CJP coverage coordinator and wrongly called his Supreme Court habeas plea a CJP filing. He filed it in his individual capacity. CJP legal cell chief Ratna Singh posted at 12:48 AM that the petition was not filed by CJP, that CJP is not approaching the Supreme Court, and that no habeas corpus petition was approved by CJP's legal team. CJP reposted her post and added "Please note." Bar & Bench and LiveLaw report that Bharti has sought to withdraw the plea. Menaka Guruswamy's separate habeas plea is unaffected.
Detention counts differ a lot by source and time. Official police figures are lower than media and CJP figures. CJP's 10,000+ is unverified.

Most detentions are preventive, not formal arrests. NDTV (~10 PM) says Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Dhruv Rathee were still in custody. Delhi Police sources (ANI, 9:38 PM) said everyone else had been released from detention centres and that CJP leaders would face due legal process. Pinarayi Vijayan, John Brittas and K.N. Balagopal (IANS, 9:20 PM), Mamata Banerjee (ANI, ~8:09 PM), Arvind Kejriwal (PTI, ~8:13 PM), Neha Bora and the women with her (India Today, ~8:30 PM) and Yogendra Yadav (his own post, 9:35 PM) were released. Ratna Singh's status is conflicting reports. No overall release count was given. As of about 10:05 PM IST. As of 11:10 PM IST, CJP says it still has no information on Dipke, Das and Ranka after 12 hours, and they remain detained. Dhruv Rathee remains detained per NDTV (~10 PM); social claims of a release are unverified. Adv Fidal Tom is alleged held at Sanjay Colony police station (Lawyers' Association for Constitution via LiveLaw and Bar & Bench). Senior Advocate Dinesh Dwivedi is detained (LiveLaw; release not reported). Yogendra Yadav says four people at Sanjay Colony police post were beaten and remain held (his claim). Delhi Metro station gates reopened around 10:36 PM (DMRC via IANS). HT (10:47 PM): police say nearly 4,000 people were detained in Delhi. As of 12:15 AM IST, NDTV says Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Dhruv Rathee remained in custody, and that all other detainees among at least 3,000 were released. HT (11:25 PM) says the same four are still held. Social claims that Dhruv Rathee has been released are unverified. Ratna Singh remains conflicting reports. Dinesh Dwivedi has no new report. A Supreme Court habeas plea seeking production of Dipke, Das and Ranka was filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity, not by CJP. LawBeat alone says it also names Rathee. As of 8:15 AM IST, Dipke, Das, Ranka and Dhruv Rathee remain detained. Ratna Singh says Dipke, Ranka and Das will be produced before an Executive Magistrate at Delhi Cantt Police Station at 9 AM; she cites a police official, and no outlet has confirmed it yet. Police sources via DNA and ET Now say over 7,000 detainees were released. CJP's claim of more than 15,000 is CJP's figure. As of 10:05 AM IST, Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka had been released at about 10 AM on an Executive Magistrate's order, and Dhruv Rathee had been released at about 3 AM. That corrects the 8:15 AM still-in-custody lines and the morning reports from ETV Bharat, ET Now and DNA. The account @CJP_for_India is not the official CJP handle. The official handle is @Cockroachisback. Statements from @CJP_for_India are unverified as CJP statements. As of 12:05 PM IST, the Supreme Court special bench had said it will pass an interim order on the Metro, free movement, the internet and lawyers, and Justice Bagchi was dictating it. The full text was not out. No CJP march or new detentions had been reported. Dipke's mother says he did not attend his grandmother's funeral.
